---
title: "Project structure and wiring"
---

`uvx capt-hook init` already wired your project: it scaffolds `.claude/hooks/` and the skills, and registers the captain-hook plugin in `.claude/settings.json` — the plugin wires every hook event by itself.

## What `init` creates

```
your-project/
├── .claude/
│   ├── hooks/
│   │   └── example.py           # the starter hook
│   ├── skills/                  # bootstrapping-hooks + translating-styleguides
│   └── settings.json            # the plugin registration (below)
```

Hooks are just Python files under `.claude/hooks/`. An optional `conf.py` beside them holds
[settings](../guide/configuration.qmd). `init` doesn't create it; add one when you need it.
`uvx capt-hook test` and `uvx capt-hook run` both default `--hooks` to that directory; pass
`--hooks <dir>` to point elsewhere.

## The wiring contract

`init` registers the captain-hook plugin in `.claude/settings.json`: an
`extraKnownMarketplaces` entry naming the marketplace and an `enabledPlugins` entry
turning the plugin on.

```json
{
  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    "captain-hook": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "yasyf/captain-hook" } }
  },
  "enabledPlugins": { "captain-hook@captain-hook": true }
}
```

The event wiring lives in the plugin itself. Its `hooks.json` registers all twelve
lifecycle events: `uvx capt-hook run <Event>` for the synchronous ones, an async
`uvx capt-hook run SessionStart --async`, and an async `uvx capt-hook review run` on
`SessionEnd` for the [session reviewer](../guide/session-reviewer.qmd). Every event is
registered up front, whether or not a hook listens on it yet; dispatch runs the hooks
that match and stays silent otherwise.

## How a hook runs

When an event fires, Claude Code runs `uvx capt-hook run <Event>` and talks to it over a pipe:

1. Claude Code writes the event as JSON to the process's **stdin**:

   ```json
   {"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "git stash"}}
   ```

2. captain-hook loads every hook in `.claude/hooks/`, runs the ones that match, and writes the
   verdict to **stdout**:

   ```json
   {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
     "permissionDecision": "deny", "permissionDecisionReason": "..."}}
   ```

3. Claude Code reads the verdict. `deny` blocks the tool, `allow` lets it through, and an
   advisory hook injects `additionalContext` instead.

## Adding hooks

Editing a hook's body needs nothing. The same `uvx capt-hook run` command picks it up.
A hook on a brand-new event needs nothing either: the plugin already registers every
event, so the new file is live from the next session, with zero settings changes.
`.claude/hooks/` is code, so commit it, and review hook changes in pull requests like
anything else.
